title: Justification is actual remission in time—not the eternal will to justify
source_text: X. Sed abutuntur illi voce Justificatio. Nam justificatio non est Dei voluntas de hominibus a peccato absolvendis, seu de remittendis homini peccatis, sed ipsa actualis remissio peccatorum, & ab iis absolutio. Atque, ut aliud est voluntas salvandi, sive sanctificandi; aliud vero salus, & sanctificatio ipsa: sic plane distingui debent, decretum seu voluntas de quibusdam justificandis & condonandis eorum peccatis; & ipsa actualis eorum justificatio, & peccati condonatio. Nam voluntas justificandi, & peccata remittendi, aeterna quidem est, & fidem praecedit: sed ipsa remissio, & justificatio in tempore fit, & fidem sequitur.
pass_a_gloss: But they abuse the word Justification. For justification is not God's will concerning people being absolved from sin, or concerning sins being remitted to a person, but the actual remission of sins itself and absolution from them. And as the will to save or sanctify is one thing, and salvation and sanctification itself another: so clearly must be distinguished the decree or will concerning certain persons to be justified and their sins forgiven, and their actual justification and the forgiveness of sin. For the will to justify and remit sins is indeed eternal and precedes faith: but the remission itself and justification happen in time and follow faith.
pass_b_english: Justification is actual remission, not the eternal will to remit.
Decree precedes faith; actual justification follows faith in time.

lemmas.gloss: happens in time and follows faith

choices.why: Means the act of remitting, not bare decree.
